written_source.anchor_text: Expand the shifted lower polynomial by the positive binomial series through coefficient \(j=2N\) and square the positive upper polynomial. Coefficients through \(j=N-1\) are the full ones. Subtract \(P_d\) and rescale by \(L^{d+1}\): the leading coefficient is \(A_{N-1}>0\); drop positive subsequent terms and bound negative terms at \(B\). Deduct the absolute \(\pi\) error using the prior sp branch at both arguments. The rescaled cost multiplies by \(L^{d+5}\); each exponential times its polynomial decreases for \(L-1>8(9+d)\), since the maximal degree including integration is \(d+8\) and rates are at least \(1/8\). The factors \(L/(L-1)\), the upper square polynomial and the unscaled error are nonincreasing. The rational check at \(B\) uses \(e>2718/1000\) and floored exponents as in the prior tail. The check margin tends to \(A_{N-1}\), the exponential costs tend to zero even after flooring, and the barrier test eventually succeeds. Thus doubling \(B\) in ramanujan_orders.py terminates for every \(d\). Binary search is only a heuristic; every reported endpoint is directly checked. Strict \(F_R>P_d\) on an explicit real ray follows at every order.

written_source.anchor_text: To justify termwise integration, choose a nonnegative smooth compactly supported weight at least 1 on any given compact interval. In the weighted squared norm of a zero-sum tail, two integrations by parts bound the kernel with phase \((\gamma-\gamma')v\) by \(C/(1+(\gamma-\gamma')^2)\), uniformly in the two real parts. FKS Lemma 2.1 and the count difference over a slightly enlarged unit bin imply \(O(\log(2+|j|))\) zeros in bin \(j\), so their sum of \(1/|\rho|\) is \(O(\log(2+|j|)/(1+|j|))\). This is a square-summable sequence. The kernel on bins is bounded by a summable multiple of \(1/(1+(j-k)^2)\); use \(a_j a_k\le(a_j^2+a_k^2)/2\) for the double sum. Thus the tail squared norms tend to zero. The local \(L^2\) limit agrees almost everywhere with the formula by the pointwise limit and a subsequence. Integration against bounded weights on compact intervals follows, also for unnormalized \(\psi(e^v)-e^v\) by multiplying by \(e^v\).

written_source.anchor_text: Platt–Trudgian arXiv:1809.03134v2 Thm. 2, PDF p. 3, prints \(n<x\le e^{58}\) and \(x\ge e^{3915}\). The literal real interpretation at the open left endpoint is false by the obstruction \((n,r]\) proved here. Dudek–Platt arXiv:1407.1901v1 Thm. 1.2, PDF p. 2, gives the older unconditional \(L\ge9658\) sign. Their Thm. 1.3 uses full RH for the ray; we reuse only the published **finite** computation: the start of §3.1, PDF p. 8, reports the largest integer counterexample up to \(10^{11}\); Lemma 3.4, PDF p. 10, gives the sieve/step interval to \(1.15\cdot10^{16}\), not its RH continuation via Lemma 3.2. These are inherited finite trust, not fresh verification. Only the integer conclusions are needed (the printed stepping discussion has endpoint rounding/strictness issues; we do not assert implementation details). On each \([j,j+1)\), \(\pi(x)\) is constant and \(ex\,\pi(x/e)/\log x\) nondecreasing for \(j>e\). The new positive bound from \(L=36.54\) overlaps the computed domain (the code checks even \(e^{36.98}<1.15\cdot10^{16}\)). Thus the real joins use neither the erroneous endpoint nor full RH.
